learning_objective: 🎯 Master the art of managing money! Understand how a business raises funds cheaply and invests them wisely to maximize wealth.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Financial management concerns the optimal procurement and usage of finance. Its primary objective is Wealth Maximisation—increasing the market value of the company's shares for shareholders.
1. Investment Decision (Capital budgeting: where to invest), 2. Financing Decision (where to raise money from: debt vs. equity), 3. Dividend Decision (how much profit to distribute vs. retain).
The mix of Debt (borrowed funds) and Equity (owners' funds). Debt is cheaper (interest is tax-deductible) but riskier. Equity is safer but more expensive.
Using more debt in the capital structure to increase the Return on Equity (ROE) for shareholders. This only works if Return on Investment (ROI) is greater than the Interest Rate on debt.
Fixed capital is invested in long-term assets (land, machinery). Working capital is used for day-to-day operations (inventory, paying salaries). High growth requires more of both.

fun_activity.title: 🍋 The Lemonade Stand CFO
fun_activity.instructions: You made $100 profit from your lemonade stand. Decide your 'Dividend Decision': How much will you keep for yourself (Dividend) and how much will you reinvest to buy a better juicer (Retained Earnings)? Why?

exam_tips: 📌 The main objective of financial management is ALWAYS 'Shareholder Wealth Maximisation', not just profit maximization.
📌 For Trading on Equity math questions: Remember ROI > Rate of Interest is the condition for it to be favorable.
📌 Financing decision focuses on the cost and risk of funds (Debt vs. Equity).
quick_recap: ⭐ Capital Budgeting decisions (long-term investments) are irreversible without massive financial loss.
⭐ Companies with stable cash flows can afford to take on more debt.
⭐ A high dividend is declared when the company has high earnings, stable cash flow, and no major investment opportunities.
